samples.summary: DOCX_ALIGNMENTS lookup walks Object.prototype, so `constructor`/`toString`/`__proto__` bypass the "closed map" and land in <w:jc w:val>
samples.evidence: `const DOCX_ALIGNMENTS: Record<string,string> = { left, center, right, justify }` is a plain object literal, so `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS[style.alignment as string]` also resolves inherited members. With `alignment === 'constructor'` the lookup returns `Object` (a function), `align !== 'left'` is true, and the exporter emits `<w:jc w:val="function Object() { [native code] }"/>`; `alignment === '__proto__'` yields `[object Object]`, `'toString'`/`'valueOf'`/`'hasOwnProperty'` similar. The whole stated purpose of the map ("can only ever carry an ST_Jc token and never an attacker-chosen fragment") is defeated for those keys. The value can reach the exporter from any CRDT writer that is not the newly-validated docs PUT (e.g. a collaborator editing the Yorkie tree directly, or slides text bodies — see the slides bypass finding). Fix: `Object.hasOwn(DOCX_ALIGNMENTS, k) ? ... : 'left'`, a Map, or `Object.create(null)`. The pre-existing `ALGN[block.style.alignment] ?? 'l'` in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79 and `UNDERLINE_STYLE_TO_U` there have the same defect.

samples.summary: New block-style value validation is bypassed by the slides arm of the same PUT endpoint (and by docs header/footer blocks)
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` is only reached from `assertValidBlock`, which is only called from `assertValidDocsBody` (line 250) and the table-cell recursion (line 322). The slides arm (`assertValidSlidesBody` → `assertValidSlide` → `assertValidElement`, lines 343-435) never inspects `element.data.textBody.blocks`, yet those blocks are docs `Block`s with `style.alignment` and are written straight into the slides CRDT by `writeSlidesRoot`, then read back by the PPTX/DOCX exporters. samples.summary: Block-style validation checks alignment values but still lets `style: {}` through, persisting the literal string "undefined" and NaN geometry into the CRDT
samples.evidence: The new test explicitly asserts `{ blocks: [{ id, type:'paragraph', style: {}, inlines: [] }] }` passes validation. `writeDocsRoot`'s `serializeBlockStyle` then produces `alignment: undefined` and `lineHeight: String(undefined) === 'undefined'` (docs-tree.ts:143-148); `parseBlockStyle` (line 159) does `Number('undefined') → NaN` and `normalizeBlockStyle` spreads that NaN over the default, so `marginTop`/`lineHeight` become NaN and `computeLayout`'s `y += block.style.marginTop` NaNs out the whole document layout. If the controller is now validating block-style *values*, the required numeric fields are the ones that actually corrupt the document when missing.

samples.summary: Run background colors were left on the raw resolver while text/underline/marker moved to resolveStoredColor
samples.evidence: `renderRun` line 421-422 (and drawInlineRunBackgroundsForLayout:234, drawInlineRunBackgroundsForPage:289, table-renderer.ts:175) still call `resolveColor(style.backgroundColor)` directly. The bare `''` case is saved by the truthiness guards, but the wrapped `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` form — which `isEmptyStoredColor` was added specifically to catch — is truthy and is handed to a theme-aware resolver, whose 'no color set' branch can return a real color and paint a fill behind text that has none. Inherited keys ('constructor', '__proto__', 'toString', 'valueOf', 'hasOwnProperty') resolve to truthy inherited members, pass the `align !== 'left'` test at :142, and are string-interpolated into `<w:jc w:val="...">` at :143 — exactly defeating the "closed map / can only ever carry an ST_Jc token" invariant asserted in the comment at :138-140. No guard elsewhere makes it unreachable, so no refutation ground applies; the broken clamp produces a schema-invalid OOXML attribute (corrupt export), a correctness/broken-invariant issue in this lens.

verdict.reason: The structural claim is accurate — assertValidBlockStyle is only reachable via assertValidBlock from assertValidDocsBody (docs-content.controller.ts:250) and the table-cell recursion (line 322), and neither the slides arm (lines 343-435) nor docs header/footer (written unvalidated at docs-tree.ts:289-303) passes through it. However, the asserted consequence is already guarded at every sink: the DOCX exporter resolves alignment through a closed map with a default (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:141, emitting <w:jc> only for mapped tokens), the PPTX exporter does the same (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79, `ALGN[...] ?? 'l'`), and the layout engine's applyAlignment simply falls through its conditionals for unknown strings (packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:887-914) without throwing. So an unvalidated alignment reaching the CRDT via the slides arm or a docs header/footer causes no crash, no 500, no data loss, and cannot be interpolated into exported XML — the only residual effect is a cosmetic right-align fallback in the renderer for a value the API arguably should reject. That is a validation-strictness/consistency gap (and, for the injection framing, the security lens's lane, where it is likewise clamped), not a blocking Correctness defect.

finding.summary: Block-style validation checks alignment values but still lets `style: {}` through, persisting the literal string "undefined" and NaN geometry into the CRDT
finding.evidence: The new test explicitly asserts `{ blocks: [{ id, type:'paragraph', style: {}, inlines: [] }] }` passes validation. `writeDocsRoot`'s `serializeBlockStyle` then produces `alignment: undefined` and `lineHeight: String(undefined) === 'undefined'` (docs-tree.ts:143-148); `parseBlockStyle` (line 159) does `Number('undefined') → NaN` and `normalizeBlockStyle` spreads that NaN over the default, so `marginTop`/`lineHeight` become NaN and `computeLayout`'s `y += block.style.marginTop` NaNs out the whole document layout. If the controller is now validating block-style *values*, the required numeric fields are the ones that actually corrupt the document when missing.

verdict.reason: Verified the whole chain in-repo and found no guard anywhere on it. (1) assertValidBlock only requires `style` to be an object (docs-content.controller.ts:292-295) and assertValidBlockStyle constrains only `alignment`, and only when defined (:266-279); the spec at docs-content.controller.spec.ts:503-514 explicitly asserts `style: {}` passes. (2) No other server-side layer catches it: `@Body() body: unknown` (:124) means the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:65) has no DTO to validate, and the body flows straight into writeDocsRoot (:164); greps for isFinite/isNaN/assertValid across packages/backend/src show no numeric block-style check. (3) serializeBlockStyle writes `alignment: undefined` and `String(undefined)` === "undefined" for lineHeight/marginTop/marginBottom/textIndent/marginLeft (docs-tree.ts:139-150) — notably NOT using the setIfDefined guard its sibling inline serializer uses (:58-66). (4) parseBlockStyle does Number("undefined") -> NaN (docs-tree.ts:157-164) and normalizeBlockStyle is a bare spread `{...DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE, ...style}` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274), so NaN overwrites defaults instead of being filtered; the frontend reader is identical (yorkie-doc-store.ts:206-227), so the live editor reads the same NaN. (5) Nothing downstream clamps: computeLayout does `y += block.style.marginTop` (packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:383) and pagination.ts:81 likewise; no isFinite guard exists on block geometry anywhere in packages/docs/src. BlockStyle declares all six fields required (types.ts:102-109), so the writer's unconditional dereference is legitimate and the API boundary is the place that must enforce them. Real and blocking under the Correctness rubric: a public PUT persists literal "undefined" strings into the shared CRDT and NaN geometry into the layout of a live collaborative document — data corruption / broken invariant on a reachable path, severity major. No counterexample found.

mergedFrom.summary: `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` lookup walks the prototype chain, so `alignment` values like `toString`/`constructor`/`valueOf` bypass the `?? 'left'` fallback

finding.summary: `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` lookup is not actually closed — prototype keys (`toString`, `constructor`, `__proto__`, `valueOf`) resolve to inherited values that get interpolated into `w:jc/@w:val`
finding.evidence: `const align = DOCX_ALIGNMENTS[style.alignment as string] ?? 'left'` indexes a plain object literal, so the prototype chain is consulted. `style.alignment === 'toString'` yields `Object.prototype.toString` (a function), which is `!== 'left'` and is stringified into `<w:jc w:val="function toString() { [native code] }"/>`; `'__proto__'` yields `[object Object]`. The doc comment above claims `w:jc w:val` "can only ever carry an ST_Jc token", which is false — the result is a schema-invalid `ST_Jc` value that Word can refuse to open, i.e. the exact failure the change set out to prevent. Use `Object.hasOwn(DOCX_ALIGNMENTS, ...)`, a `Map`/`Set`, or `Object.create(null)`. The same pattern exists in the slides sink the comment cites as the model (`packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79`, `ALGN[block.style.alignment] ?? 'l'`), so it is not clamped there either.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: DOCX_ALIGNMENTS (docx-style-map.ts:115-120) is a plain object literal and is read with bracket access at line 141 (`DOCX_ALIGNMENTS[style.alignment as string] ?? 'left'`), so inherited prototype keys ('toString', 'valueOf', 'constructor', '__proto__') resolve to truthy non-'left' values that bypass both the `??` fallback and the `align !== 'left'` check and are template-interpolated unescaped into `<w:jc w:val="...">` at line 143 — contradicting the comment at lines 111-113/138-140 that the map is closed. The path is reachable: the only value-level allowlist is the REST-only `assertValidBlockStyle`/`BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS` Set (docs-content.controller.ts:254,266-279), while the CRDT read paths cast unchecked (yorkie/docs-tree.ts:157-164 and frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:220) and `normalizeBlockStyle` (model/types.ts:272-274) is a plain spread with no validation, so an arbitrary alignment string persisted via collaboration flows into docx-exporter.ts:186 and out into word/document.xml as an invalid ST_Jc token. Existing test coverage (docx-style-map.test.ts:149-158) only exercises a quote-injection string, not prototype keys. Real broken-invariant/incomplete-guard defect in the correctness lane; no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: New block-style value validation covers only `alignment`; the numeric BlockStyle fields still accept arbitrary values that become NaN in layout
finding.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` validates `style.alignment` only. `writeDocsRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:145) writes `marginTop: String(style.marginTop)` verbatim, and the read path does `partial.marginTop = Number(attrs.marginTop)` (docs-tree.ts:160) with `normalizeBlockStyle` being a bare spread (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274, no numeric coercion/guard). A PUT with `style: { marginTop: "abc" }` therefore lands NaN in the model, and `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:383` does `y += block.style.marginTop`, NaN-ing the cumulative y for every subsequent block — the whole document renders blank/garbled for every collaborator, with no way to fix it from the UI. Same exposure for `marginBottom`, `lineHeight`, `textIndent`, `marginLeft`.

verdict.reason: Verified every hop and found no guard. assertValidBlockStyle (docs-content.controller.ts:266-279) validates only style.alignment; assertValidBlock (:292-295) requires style to be an object only. writeDocsRoot -> buildBlockNode -> serializeBlockStyle (docs-tree.ts:139-149, called at :241/:258) stringifies marginTop/marginBottom/lineHeight/textIndent/marginLeft verbatim from the request body (controller :164). Both read paths (docs-tree.ts:152-165 and frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:217-227) do Number(attrs.x) with no finiteness check, and normalizeBlockStyle is a bare spread (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274) so an explicit NaN overrides the default instead of being replaced. Sink layout.ts:383 does y += block.style.marginTop inside the block loop, so one NaN poisons cumulative y for all later blocks; :741 Math.max(1, lineHeight ?? 1.5) also yields NaN since ?? does not catch NaN. Tellingly, the very same files guard the analogous numeric case for images with Number.isFinite (docs-tree.ts:121-126, yorkie-doc-store.ts:186-191), so the omission here is not covered elsewhere. Searches across packages/docs/src and packages/frontend/src/app/docs for isFinite/isNaN/sanitiz/migrate turned up no block-style numeric normalization, and materializeBlockSpacing/resolveStyleBlock (named-styles.ts:133-151) are plain spreads not on the computeLayout path. The controller spec (docs-content.controller.spec.ts:484-501) shows alignment-only intent with no numeric test. Blocking under Correctness: an accepted PUT persists a broken invariant into the CRDT that garbles rendering for every collaborator with no UI recovery.

finding.summary: Cell-style attribute removal uses a *range* over the whole cell subtree, so `backgroundColor` is also stripped from every inline (text highlight) and nested-table node inside the cell
finding.evidence: `applyCellStyle` now does `tree.removeStyleByPath(cellPath, endPath, removeAttrs)` with `endPath = [...cellPath]` and last index +1 — a position range that spans the cell node AND all of its descendants (blocks, inlines, nested tables). Yorkie's tree style/removeStyle applies to every non-text node in the range (the same reason `setBlockType`'s `removeStyleByPath(blockPath, blockPath+1, ['listKind','listLevel'])` at line 1439 reaches inline nodes too — harmlessly, because those keys don't exist there). Here the attribute name collides: inline nodes store text highlight under the very same key `backgroundColor` (`serializeInlineStyle` line 122, `parseInlineStyle` line 177), and nested table cells store `backgroundColor`/`border*`/`padding`. So the new "No fill" reset (docs-table-context-menu.tsx:233 → `{ backgroundColor: undefined }`) silently deletes the highlight colour of every run in the cell and the fills/borders of any nested table — irreversible data loss in the CRDT. The in-memory cache is only patched for the cell (`cell.style = merged`), so the loss is invisible until reload/remote sync, and the added test (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2031) uses a cell whose inlines have no `backgroundColor`, so it cannot catch this. A per-node removal (or an explicit `removeStyleByPath` restricted to the cell element only, e.g. by re-setting the descendants' attrs) is needed.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. applyCellStyle sets attributes with a single-path styleByPath (cell node only) at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2447 but removes them over a range spanning the whole cell subtree at :2448-2452 (endPath = cellPath with last index +1, i.e. the next sibling cell). removedCellStyleAttrs (:255-261) yields 'backgroundColor', 'padding', 'border*', which collide with inline attribute names written by serializeInlineStyle:122 and read by parseInlineStyle:177; inlines are descendants of the cell (buildCellNode:344-350 -> buildBlockNode:337-341). Yorkie's tree style/removeStyle applies to every non-text node in the range, which this file itself acknowledges by doing per-inline removeStyleByPath in applyStyle (:1892-1897) instead of a whole-block range; the identical whole-cell range in applyCellSpan (:2500-2504) is harmless only because colSpan/rowSpan don't exist on descendants. The path is user-reachable: docs-table-context-menu.tsx:233 ('Reset'/no-fill) -> editor.ts:3648-3671 -> document.ts:856-861 -> store, looping over every selected cell (editor.ts:3657-3661). No guard prevents it; the cache is patched only for the cell (:2456), so the loss of inline highlight colours (and nested-cell fills/borders) lands in the CRDT and only becomes visible after reload/remote sync. The added test (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2033-2047) uses cells whose inlines carry no backgroundColor, so it cannot catch it. This is data loss on a real path -> blocking under the correctness rubric.
